test_evidence.details: Untouched pre-change Go baseline passed in the official Go 1.23 container. The host has no Go executable, so the container is the reproducible test runtime.
Untouched pre-change React baseline passed: 1 suite and 1 test. It emitted the existing TitleComponent componentWillMount warning.

Final uncached source characterization passed. It covers real JWT/JWKS middleware for missing, malformed, valid, matching, mismatched, expired, wrong-audience, and missing-subject credentials; feelings and weekly success/empty/invalid/identity/query/upsert behavior through real Gin handlers with Mongo wire mocks; and legacy CORS plus unmatched ping behavior.

Final React suite passed: 2 suites and 3 tests. New tests verify current Auth0 audience, bearer and x-user-id headers, routes, query parameters, and feelings/weekly request payloads. The pre-existing TitleComponent lifecycle warning remains characterized and unchanged.
The base-URL-driven source/target smoke runner is syntactically valid. It requires explicit CONTRACT_BASE_URL and optional isolated test credentials at execution time and embeds no credentials.
Runtime-neutral contract fixtures are valid JSON and contain only synthetic identities and content.
The source plan remained structurally valid, ready, and approved while Stage 1 was implemented.

stages.notes: Stage 1 changed tests, test-only module metadata, fixtures, and migration documentation only; server/main.go, server/handlers.go, and runtime React behavior were not modified. Characterized source quirks include null empty feelings, unsorted feeling reads, permissive/inconsistent validation errors, empty-200 CORS rejection, and an unmatched client ping. The replacement must follow the approved normalized design rather than copy those quirks. Repository search plus Vinicius Delascio's Define-stage confirmation provides the current evidence that the OpenClaw/chat/agent routes have no caller; no production logs, secrets, private data, or external systems were accessed.

test_evidence.details: Pinned runtime reports Deno 2.9.4 stable, V8 15.0.245.2-rusty, and TypeScript 6.0.3. The official image resolves to denoland/deno@sha256:c777b4b225501a61074837e90a826a58f99124837824023cd60334b1e2374498.
Deno formatter checked all eight Stage 2 source, test, configuration, and documentation files with no differences.
Deno lint checked all six TypeScript source and test files with no findings.
Frozen dependency resolution and TypeScript checking passed for src/main.ts and all tests.

Seven tests passed. They verify the health-only HTTP surface, absence of business and retired routes, strict Zod schemas, JOSE signing/verification and remote-JWKS support, lazy TLS postgres.js compatibility with prepared statements disabled, strict runtime configuration, and log field redaction.
Deno reported no known vulnerabilities in the lockfile. The lock contains only the three explicit zero-transitive-dependency packages: Zod 4.4.3, JOSE 6.2.9, and postgres.js 3.4.9.

A clean OCI build passed from the digest-pinned official Deno image using deno ci --prod, the frozen integrity lockfile, and an in-image type check. No lifecycle scripts, node_modules directory, native addons, or unpinned base tag are required.
The final local container returned HTTP 200, cache-control no-store, application/json, and {"status":"ok"}.
The final image ran as uid/gid 1993 (deno).

The final command uses frozen cached dependencies, no prompts, environment access only for DEPLOYMENT_VERSION/HOST/PORT, ignored ambient PG* reads, and network permission only to listen on 0.0.0.0:8080; no filesystem, subprocess, FFI, system, or broad environment permission is granted.

SIGTERM produced sanitized server_shutdown_started and server_shutdown_complete JSON events and the ephemeral container exited cleanly. Startup and health request logs contained only allowlisted operational fields.

The unchanged legacy Go API and React production image still builds after adding the root .dockerignore, preserving the rollback source. Its existing npm dependency installation reported 82 audit findings (15 low, 17 moderate, 42 high, and 8 critical); Stage 2 did not alter or waive them.

stages.notes: Stage 2 selects native Deno.serve rather than an HTTP framework, native Deno.test with node:assert/strict, Zod 4.4.3, JOSE 6.2.9, and postgres.js 3.4.9. Deno config-file permission sets were evaluated but not retained because Deno 2.9 still marks them experimental; stable explicit CLI permissions provide the approved least-privilege boundary. postgres.js probes conventional PG* environment names even with an explicit URL, so those reads are explicitly ignored rather than granted. The foundation exposes only GET /healthz and structured allowlisted logs. Auth0 middleware, real database connectivity, feelings, weekly tracker, Data API, Edge Functions, Storage, jobs, and operator behavior remain unimplemented. No Supabase resource, cloud infrastructure, credential, production data, environment, endpoint, or traffic was accessed or changed.
